subject: English Language
text: Neither the principal nor the students ____ prepared for the inspection.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'students' is plural so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By this time next year, I ____ my apprenticeship.
explanation: Use the future perfect 'will have completed' to show an action finished before a specified future time.

subject: English Language
text: She felt a deep sense of ____ when she returned to her childhood home.
explanation: Nostalgia means a longing for the past, which matches returning to a childhood home; other choices conflict in meaning.

subject: English Language
text: He has a lot on his plate.
options: He has many tasks to handle.
explanation: The idiom 'has a lot on his plate' means being busy or overloaded with tasks; the first option accurately paraphrases it.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correct for: He said 'i will arrive at noon'.
options: He said, "I will arrive at noon."
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Correct punctuation: comma before direct speech, capital 'I', and the full stop inside closing quotation marks; semicolon is incorrect.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has primary stress in the word "photograph"?
explanation: The noun 'photograph' has primary stress on the first syllable: 'PHO-to-graph'. Stress rules place main stress on the first syllable here.

subject: English Language
text: Teacher: "Could you please switch off your phone?" Student reply:
options: No, I won't switch it off.
Sorry, I'll switch it off now.
Why should I switch it off?
explanation: Polite request requires a polite, compliant response; 'Sorry, I'll switch it off now.' acknowledges and fulfils the request.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: "The committee chose Amaka as secretary."
options: Amaka chose as secretary by the committee.
Amaka was chosen by the committee as secretaryed.
Amaka had chosen the committee as secretary.
Amaka was chosen as secretary by the committee.
explanation: Passive requires 'be' + past participle: 'Amaka was chosen'; agent can follow with 'by the committee'. Other options are ungrammatical.

subject: English Language
text: We must make room ____ innovative suggestions at the meeting.
explanation: 'Make room for' is the correct collocation meaning to allow space or opportunity; other prepositions do not fit this collocation.

subject: English Language
text: Amina watered the saplings every evening. Yet only a few survived the dry season.
options: Amina's care was the reason many plants died.
The drought was severe despite Amina's care.
The saplings were already mature trees.
Amina overwatered the saplings and killed them.
explanation: The best inference is that environmental conditions (a severe dry season) overcame her care; it does not blame her actions directly.

subject: English Language
text: Each of the students ____ a copy of the handbook.
explanation: Use singular verb after 'Each of the ...' because 'each' is singular; therefore 'has' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the exam starts, I ____ the revision.
explanation: Future perfect expresses completion before a future time: 'will have completed' shows the revision finished before the exam starts.

subject: English Language
text: We should insist ____ a refund for the faulty radio.
explanation: The verb 'insist' collocates with the preposition 'on' when demanding something: 'insist on a refund' is standard usage.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correct for the sentence: Peter shouted, "the bus is leaving now."
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
Peter shouted, "The bus is leaving now."
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct speech begins with a capital letter and normally follows a comma after the reporting verb: comma + capitalised quote is correct.

subject: English Language
text: When the manager said 'we are in the same boat', she meant:
options: they were on a boat together
explanation: The idiom 'in the same boat' means sharing similar difficulties or problems, not a literal boat or uniform.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: "The teacher will announce the results tomorrow."
options: Tomorrow the results will announce by the teacher.
The results were announced by the teacher tomorrow.
The teacher will be announcing the results tomorrow by.
The results will be announced by the teacher tomorrow.
explanation: Passive requires object as subject plus correct auxiliary: 'The results will be announced by the teacher tomorrow.' matches future passive form.

subject: English Language
text: Kemi had never seen _____ elephant before the zoo trip.
explanation: Before a singular noun beginning with vowel sound 'e' we use the indefinite article 'an': 'an elephant' is grammatically correct.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has primary stress in the word 'economy'?
explanation: The word 'economy' is pronounced e-CON-o-my; primary stress falls on the second syllable 'con'.

subject: English Language
text: Teacher: "Could you hand me the chalk?" Student reply:
explanation: A polite, direct fulfilment of the request is 'Certainly, here it is.' which appropriately hands over the chalk.

subject: English Language
text: Richard left early with a packed lunch and a bottle of water.
options: He intended to host a picnic at home.
He was punctually going to school.
He planned to stay away for some hours.
explanation: Taking a packed lunch and water suggests planning to be away for several hours; this inference follows from the items he carried.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the coach nor the players ____ willing to postpone the match.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer noun ('players' plural), so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By the time she graduates, she ____ at the university for four years.
explanation: The future perfect continuous (will have been studying) shows duration up to a future point.

subject: English Language
text: Mr. Idris is admired in the village for his probity.
explanation: Probity means integrity or honesty; the other choices are semantically different qualities.

subject: English Language
text: When Yara said she would 'eat humble pie', she meant she would:
explanation: 'Eat humble pie' is an idiom meaning to admit error and apologise; literal meanings are incorrect.

subject: English Language
text: Which is the correctly punctuated version of the sentence: "Listen said aunty, we must leave now."
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct speech needs commas inside quotes, Aunty is a proper noun here and must be capitalised.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has primary stress in the word 'dictionary'?
explanation: Dictionary is pronounced 'DIC-tion-a-ry' with primary stress on the first syllable (DIC-).

subject: English Language
text: Choose the word that has a different vowel sound from the others: ship, chip, sheep, dip.
explanation: 'Sheep' has the long vowel /i:/, while 'ship', 'chip' and 'dip' have the short /ɪ/ vowel sound.

subject: English Language
text:
Teacher: "Could you fetch the register?"
Which student reply is the most appropriate spoken response?
explanation: 'Could you' is a polite request; a suitable immediate acceptance is 'Yes, I'll fetch it.'

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: "The janitor cleans the hall every morning."
options: The hall is cleaned by the janitor every morning.
The hall was cleaned by the janitor every morning.
Every morning the hall is being cleaned by the janitor.
The janitor is cleaned the hall every morning.
explanation: Present simple passive uses 'is/are' + past participle: 'The hall is cleaned by the janitor every morning.'

subject: English Language
text: The scientist's theory was controversial, but her data gave it considerable ____.
explanation: Credence means acceptance or belief; 'gave it credence' is the correct collocation; others are unrelated.

subject: English Language
text: Either the librarian or the students ____ responsible for rearranging the shelves.
explanation: With 'either...or' the verb agrees with the noun nearest it; 'students' is plural so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By November, I ____ on the coastal survey for three months.
explanation: Future perfect continuous (will have been + -ing) expresses duration up to a specified future time: 'will have been working'.

subject: English Language
topic: Lexis and semantics (Word choice for brevity)
text: Ruth's reply was terse; she offered no further ____.
explanation: A terse reply lacks extra detail; 'elaboration' (further detail or development) best fits the contrast.

subject: English Language
text: When the manager told him to 'bite the bullet', she meant he should:
options: tell an untruth to get by
accept and endure the difficult task
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' is an idiom meaning to accept and endure something unpleasant rather than avoid it.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is punctuated correctly for: The governor said 'we will rebuild the bridge'.
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The governor said, "We will rebuild the bridge."
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct speech needs a comma before the quotation and the quoted sentence begins with a capital letter; proper nouns not needed in 'bridge'.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has primary stress in the word 'photographer'?
explanation: Pronunciation: pho-TOG-ra-pher has primary stress on the second syllable 'TOG' (contrast with 'photograph' stressed on the first).

subject: English Language
text: Teacher: "Please hand in your homework now." Which student reply is most appropriate?
options: I refuse to hand it in.
I lost it, but I might find it later.
explanation: Polite compliance suits the teacher's request; 'Here is my homework, sir.' shows appropriate, succinct spoken response.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: "They will deliver the textbooks on Monday."
options: On Monday the textbooks will deliver.
The textbooks will be delivered on Monday.
The textbooks will deliver on Monday.
Textbooks will be delivered by they on Monday.
explanation: Passive uses object as subject plus 'be' + past participle: 'The textbooks will be delivered on Monday.' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: She congratulated him ____ securing the scholarship.
explanation: Verb+preposition collocation: 'congratulate someone on (something)' is the correct pattern, so use 'on'.

subject: English Language
text: Amina kept the old clock as a memento of her aunt. The clock rarely worked, but she checked it often. What inference is best?
options: She believed the clock would increase in market value.
She used the clock as her main way of telling time.
She resented her aunt's taste in objects.
She valued the clock for emotional reasons.
explanation: The facts imply sentimental attachment: keeping a non-working clock and checking it often indicates emotional value rather than monetary or practical use.

subject: English Language
text: By midnight tomorrow, I ____ the annual report.
explanation: Use future perfect ('will have completed') for an action finished before a stated future time.

subject: English Language
text: A pair of scissors ____ on the workbench.
explanation: The head noun 'pair' is singular so the verb takes singular agreement: 'A pair ... is'. This differs from plural nouns.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has primary stress in the word 'comfortable'?
explanation: 'Comfortable' is stressed on the first syllable: COM-fort-a-ble. Primary stress falls on 'COM'.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the word that has a different vowel sound from the others: book, cook, boot, look.
explanation: 'book', 'cook', 'look' use /ʊ/ while 'boot' uses /uː/; thus 'boot' has a different vowel quality.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is punctuated correctly for the sentence: The head said 'close the doors now'.
options: The head said, "Close the doors now."
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct quotation of a full sentence needs a comma before the quote and a capital letter inside: The head said, "Close the doors now." Punctuation stays inside the quotation marks.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: "The gardener will plant the mango trees next week."
options: The mango trees will be planting by the gardener next week.
The mango trees will be planted by the gardener next week.
The gardener will have the mango trees planted next week.
Next week the gardener will be planting the mango trees.
explanation: Passive of 'will plant' is 'will be planted'; retain agent with 'by the gardener' and time phrase remains at end.

subject: English Language
text: We must guard public funds ____ misuse.
explanation: Collocation requires 'guard (something) from (harm)': 'guard public funds from misuse' is the correct prepositional choice.

subject: English Language
text: When the director told the team to 'keep investors at arm's length', she meant:
options: Arrange physical seating to keep them away.
Invite them to join every meeting.
explanation: The idiom 'keep someone at arm's length' means to maintain a cautious or distant relationship, not literal distance or openness.

subject: English Language
text: Teacher: "Please summarise your answer in one sentence." Which student reply is most appropriate?
explanation: The teacher requests an action; an appropriate spoken reply is polite acceptance: 'Okay, I will do that.' This matches the speech function.

subject: English Language
text: Amaka kept a faded concert ticket in her diary and read the date every year, though she never attended that show again. What is the best inference?
options: She lost interest in attending concerts.
She cherished the memory of that event.
She could no longer afford tickets.
She used the ticket as a bookmark.
explanation: Keeping and revisiting a memento annually indicates sentimental value; the behaviour supports cherishing a memory rather than the other options.
